title: Boss: works on my machine
summary: Sam's status page config fails three different ways on a clean machine. Read each error, find the cause, and leave it applying cleanly with a plan that stays quiet.

steps.title: Ticket PLAT-118
body: *"Sam is on holiday and the status page needs a new deploy. The repo is `~/infra/status-page`. The README says
init, plan, apply. It does not work for me. Also, Sam mentioned the plan 'always shows something', is that normal?"*
Three stages, one bug each. Start from the **first error message** every time: read the block it names, the line,
and the sentence under it. Every check runs real Terraform on what you leave behind.

steps.title: init fails
prompt: `cd ~/infra/status-page && terraform init` fails. Read the error, fix the configuration (not the machine), and get
`init` and `terraform validate` to succeed. The machine's provider mirror is what an air-gapped company network has:

checks.name: init has installed the providers
checks.fail: `terraform init` has not installed `hashicorp/random` yet (no entry in `.terraform.lock.hcl`). Fix the version constraint it complains about.

checks.name: the constraint allows a current 3.x
checks.fail: `versions.tf` still asks for `~> 3.6.0`, a version that is not available.

checks.name: validate passes
checks.fail: `terraform validate` should succeed (it needs a successful init).

hints: The error: `no available releases match the given constraints ~> 3.6.0`. What does `~> 3.6.0` allow?
`~> 3.6.0` means 3.6.x only. The mirror has 3.7.2 and 3.9.1. A constraint like `~> 3.9` allows any 3.x from 3.9.
steps.explain: A too-tight constraint is a common reason a config only works where it was first initialised: Sam's laptop still had 3.6 in its cache. With a public registry the same error appears when a version was yanked, or when a module asks for a range that does not overlap with yours (`terraform providers` shows who asks for what).

steps.title: Unsupported attribute
prompt: `init` works now, but `terraform plan` fails with **Unsupported attribute**. Find out which attributes `random_pet`
really exports (the provider's schema is on this machine: `terraform providers schema -json | jq` on

checks.name: the page shows the build name
checks.cmd:
cd ~/infra/status-page && grep -q "

Build $(terraform state show -no-color random_pet.page | sed -n 's/^ *id *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/p')

" public/index.html
checks.fail:
`public/index.html` should contain `

Build

`. Fix the reference and apply.

hints: The error points at `random_pet.page.name`: there is no exported attribute called `name`.

`terraform providers schema -json | jq '.provider_schemas["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/random"].resource_schemas.random_pet.block.attributes | keys'` lists `id`, `keepers`, `length`, `prefix`, `separator`. The generated name is the `id`.
`sed -i 's/random_pet.page.name/random_pet.page.id/' main.tf`, then `terraform plan -out=tfplan` and `terraform apply tfplan`.
steps.explain: Each provider documents its attributes on the Terraform Registry, but the schema on your machine is the truth for the exact version you run. `terraform providers schema -json` is how editors and linters know it too.

steps.title: The plan that always shows something
prompt: Sam's comment was right: it is applied, and yet **every** `terraform plan` wants to replace `local_file.index`. A plan
that is never empty hides real changes and breaks drift alerts.
1. Plan twice and compare. Which expression is never the same twice?
2. Keep the *Last deployed* line, but make it change only when the page really changes: record the time once, in the
state, with a `time_static` resource from the `hashicorp/time` provider (add it to `required_providers`, version
3. Apply, then show that `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` exits 0.

checks.name: no timestamp() left
checks.fail: `timestamp()` returns the current time on every plan, so the content is never the same. Replace it.

checks.name: a time_static records the deploy time
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/status-page && t=$(terraform state show -no-color "$(terraform state list | grep '^time_static\.' | head -n1)" | sed -n 's/^ *rfc3339 *= *"\(.*\)"/\1/p') && test -n "$t" && grep -q "Last deployed: $t" public/index.html
checks.fail: `public/index.html` should say `Last deployed: <the rfc3339 of a time_static resource in the state>`.

checks.name: two plans in a row show no changes
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/status-page && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color >/dev/null && sleep 1 && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color >/dev/null
checks.fail: `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` should exit 0, twice in a row.

hints: `timestamp()` is evaluated on every plan, so `content` changes every time, and a file's content forces replacement.

Add `time = { source = "hashicorp/time", version = "~> 0.14" }` to `required_providers`, a `resource "time_static" "deployed" {}` block, and use `${time_static.deployed.rfc3339}`. Run `terraform init` again for the new provider.

`sed -i 's/timestamp()/time_static.deployed.rfc3339/' main.tf`, `printf 'resource "time_static" "deployed" {}\n' >> main.tf`, `sed -i '/hashicorp\/random/a\    time   = { source = "hashicorp/time", version = "~> 0.14" }' versions.tf`, then init, plan, apply.
steps.explain: `timestamp()`, `uuid()` and reading files that change on every run all produce a *perpetual diff*. `time_static` stores the time once in the state; it only changes when you replace it (for example with `triggers` or `replace_triggered_by`, module 3). A quiet plan is a feature: it means any change you see is real.
